# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Model in use does not update in Pi plugin

## Headline

The Worklog Pi extension footer (Line 3, right-aligned) shows a stale "model in use" after a mid-session model switch: the newly selected alias is paired with the previous session's resolved provider/model until the next Local Proxy response arrives — and permanently so when the switched-to model is not proxy-routed (e.g. a direct `deepseek` or `opencode` provider), because the `X-Resolved-Model` header never arrives. Intake RCA: `_resolvedModel` is never invalidated on `model_select` (only on `session_start`).

## Problem statement

After `/model` (or model cycling) mid-session, the footer's resolved provider/model does not update properly — it keeps showing the previously resolved model instead of the newly selected one. Root cause (confirmed by code reading): in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts`, the resolved value (`_resolvedModel`) is only ever (a) set from the Local Proxy `X-Resolved-Model` response header in `after_provider_response`, or (b) reset to `null` on `session_start` (see WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6). The `model_select` handler updates only `_selectedModel`. Two observable outcomes:

1. Immediately after a switch, the footer shows `newAlias → oldResolvedModel` (stale/misleading) until the first response carrying a new header arrives.
2. If the switched-to model is served by a non-proxy provider (`deepseek`, `opencode` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`) no `X-Resolved-Model` header ever arrives, so the stale value persists for the rest of the session — or, if we only cleared the cache, the footer would show `(resolving)` forever, which is equally wrong.

## Users

- **Pi operator** switching models mid-session (e.g. `code` → `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) to control cost/latency: needs the footer to reflect the switch immediately so they trust which model is actually serving the session.
  - *User story:* "When I run `/model` to switch to a cheaper or local model, I expect the footer to show the new model right away — not the old one — and definitely not forever."
- **Producer/auditor** reviewing recorded sessions: the displayed model must be trustworthy for RCA and cost attribution.
  - *User story:* "I check the footer to confirm which model handled a turn; a stale label makes the record unreliable."

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `model_select` fires mid-session (sources `set` and `cycle`), the previously resolved model is immediately invalidated: `getResolvedModel()` returns `null` right after the handler runs and the footer shows `<newAlias> → (resolving)` until a fresh proxy response arrives. Unit-testable in `model-display.test.ts` and a footer-render regression test in `session-health.test.ts`.
- When the selected model's provider is not the Local Proxy (no `X-Resolved-Model` header can arrive), the footer displays the model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of a stale proxy value or an unbounded `(resolving)` state. The proxy provider is identified by name (`Local Proxy`) — the same convention already centralised in `@worklog/shared/lease-release` (`LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME`).
- Subsequent proxy responses update the resolved value exactly as today (header extraction, uppercase/lowercase handling, no-op on identical values, `onModelChange` firing) — no regression to existing behaviour covered by `model-display.test.ts`.
- The fix is fail-open when config is unavailable/unknown (no throw, no crash); existing `(resolving)`, right-alignment, and width-handling behaviour on Footer Line 3 (WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P, WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP, WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5) is preserved.
- At least one unit test covers the end-to-end footer rendering for a mid-session switch (new alias + invalidation) and for the non-proxy provider case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (`packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — "Model/Provider Display (Line 3)" state table and the `model_select` event-row meaning), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Changes are confined to the Worklog Pi extension package (`packages/tui/extensions`); no local-proxy changes (the proxy already emits `x-resolved-model` on every response it routes — verified by the earlier spike SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 and a live probe).
- Must preserve the intermediate `(resolving)` state introduced by WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P and the session-start reset fix (WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6) — this work is the mid-session analogue of that fix.
- Non-TUI modes must keep degrading gracefully (footer is a no-op outside TUI).
- Keep the fix surgical: no speculative refactor of the model-display module.

## Existing state

- `model-display.ts` (6222 B): module-level `_resolvedModel` / `_selectedModel`; `_onModelChange` is a **single callback slot** (multi-subscriber clobbering is a latent defect but not currently triggered). Listeners: `session_start` (resets `_resolvedModel`, seeds `_selectedModel` if unset), `model_select` (sets `_selectedModel` only), `after_provider_response` (sets `_resolvedModel` from `x-resolved-model`/`X-Resolved-Model` header only when it differs).
- `session-health.ts` (Line 3 render): `${selectedModel} → ${resolvedModel}`, else `alias → (resolving)`, else `resolvedModel`, else `—`. Subscribes via `onModelChange(() => tui.requestRender())` on first render.
- Pi SDK: `model_select` event carries `{ model: {provider, id}, previousModel, source: "set"|"cycle"|"restore" }` and fires on `/model`, model cycling, and session restore (verified in `pi-coding-agent` types `ModelSelectEvent` and `examples/extensions/model-status.ts`). `after_provider_response` exposes the raw HTTP response headers (lowercase-normalised).
- Proxy provider config lives in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; the project already centralises the `Local Proxy` provider-name constant and models.json lookup in `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts`.

## Desired change

1. In the `model_select` handler of `model-display.ts`: invalidate `_resolvedModel` (set `null`) and notify `_onModelChange` so the footer re-renders to `newAlias → (resolving)`.
2. If the newly selected model's provider is not the configured Local Proxy provider, treat the model's own `provider/id` as the resolved value immediately (no `(resolving)` limbo), so the footer shows the true model.
3. No change to the render logic in `session-health.ts` is expected (it already handles `null` resolved); add only regression tests. If a change becomes necessary it must keep the existing right-align and width-budget behaviour.
4. Update `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` to document the mid-session invalidation and the non-proxy fallback in the state table.

## Key Files:

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` — invalidate `_resolvedModel` on `model_select`; derive `provider/id` fallback for non-proxy providers.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.test.ts` — new tests: mid-session switch invalidation (all sources), non-proxy fallback, no regression to header extraction.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — footer Line 3 render regression test for mid-session switch and non-proxy provider.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — verify only (render already null-aware); touch only if tests reveal otherwise.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document updated `model_select` semantics and new fallback display.
- (reference, not changed) `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` — canonical `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` convention to reuse.

## Related work

- WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 (completed) — Reset resolved model on session_start to avoid stale display across sessions. **Direct sibling:** same stale-display class; fixed at session boundary only, leaving the mid-session hole this item covers.
- WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P (completed) — Show model status in pi quickly; introduced the `(resolving)` intermediate state.
- WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0 / WL-0MRF19R71004YJND (completed) — Session Health footer and the Line-3 model/provider line.
- WL-0MRC3F30E008XJN3 / WL-0MRC91VIN0089UXD / WL-0MRC3NOVZ000P0P5 (completed) — Model-display extension integration into the Worklog extension (status-line provenance).
- WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP, WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 (completed) — Line-3 right-alignment/truncation and alias/command position swaps that must not regress.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risks**
  - Header-based resolution remains the single source of truth for proxy-routed models; if a switch does not produce a new header (identical downstream model, request failure, non-proxy fallback routes), the footer can still lag. Mitigation: AC2 shows the selected model's own `provider/id` for non-proxy providers; `(resolving)` is the honest state while a proxy response is pending.
  - Some providers in `models.json` run under `modelOverrides` (e.g. `opencode`); deriving `${provider}/${id}` must use the *selected* model's provider/id, not overrides, to stay truthful.
  - Scope-creep risk: do not also "fix" the single-slot `onModelChange` (latent, no current trigger) or alias staleness on `session_start` guard (`! _selectedModel`) in this item — record as `discovered-from` follow-ups instead if the implementer confirms they are real.
- **Assumptions (documented, communicated on completion)**
  - A1. The observed defect is the stale resolved model after a mid-session switch, in both proxy and non-proxy scenarios (the only code path consistent with "does not update properly").
  - A2. The proxy provider is identified by the literal name `Local Proxy` (project convention in `lease-release.ts`); no config re-read is required if the check is by provider name against the constant, otherwise reuse the shared models.json lookup.
  - A3. On any mid-session `model_select` (including `restore`), invalidating the resolved value is correct; `session_start` already resets at session boundaries.
- **Open confirmation questions for the producer (non-blocking — see Appendix)**

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What exactly did you observe when changing the model mid-session — did the left-hand alias update while the right-hand resolved model stayed on the previous one (or until the next turn), or did the whole label fail to change?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded for producer confirmation). Research: the code only updates the resolved half from the `X-Resolved-Model` response header and invalidates it only on `session_start`, so the stale-resolved/lagging scenarios are the only code-consistent outcomes. Assumption A1 covers both.
- Q2: "When the switched-to model is NOT served by the Local Proxy (e.g. direct `deepseek`/`opencode` providers in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`), should the footer show the selected model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of an endless `(resolving)`?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — Recommended: yes** (shows the true serving model; `(resolving)` forever is untruthful). Assumption A2.
- Q3: "Should invalidating the resolved value also apply when the model is restored/re-selected at session start (`source: restore`), consistent with the WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 session-start reset?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — Recommended: yes** (uniform behaviour; `session_start` already resets). Assumption A3.

  Research summary: pi's `model_select` events carry `model.provider`/`model.id` and `source` (`set|cycle|restore`); `after_provider_response` carries the raw HTTP headers and the Local Proxy adds `x-resolved-model` on the responses it routes (live-verified in spike SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0). No new pi-version of the SDK contract is required.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRC3NOVZ000P0P5** – Model display extension is not showing the provider (completed)
- **WL-0MRC91VIN0089UXD** – Move provider/model display to start of Worklog extension status line (completed)
- **WL-0MRE6JDT3004OSTF** – proactively release leases (completed)

### Repository file matches
Automated repo-file matches were reviewed and discarded as keyword noise (the full untruncated report is retained at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB.md`). The high-signal related files are listed under **Key Files** above.


## Plan: changelog

## Failure Signature

- Test name: `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` > read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) > cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh
- Failure type: **timeout**, not an assertion failure — the test never reached its ≥60% assertion
- Failing commit: (not available) — observed in a post-push full-suite run on `dev`, 2026-10-20
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Error: Test timed out in 300000ms. If this is a long-running test, pass a timeout value as the last argument or configure it globally with testTimeout.
```

### Verified during planning (2026-10-20, `dev` @ `bec96e2b`)

- **The failure is wall-clock, not behavioural.** The test's own budget is
  already `300_000` ms (`it(..., 300_000)`) and the seeding `beforeEach` hook
  has `180_000` ms. Exceeding 300 s means no assertion executed, so this
  evidence does **not** implicate the read-cache reduction behaviour — only
  the test's cost.
- **Independent timing baseline.** `test-timings.json`
  (generated 2026-10-20T05:04:37Z) records this test at **203 188 ms
  (203 s)** — the slowest single test in the repository, ahead of
  `sync-vs-mutation` (163 s) and `read-cache-e2e` (146 s).
- **Spawn arithmetic.** The test performs 5 seeding
  `tsx src/cli.ts create` subprocesses + the baseline phase (6 panes × 5
  queries = 30) + the cached phase (6 panes × 5 queries = 30) = **65 `tsx`
  subprocesses**, each a cold Node + tsx start (~3 s average at the recorded
  203 s total).
- **Contention amplifier.** `vitest.config.ts` runs `pool: 'forks'` with
  `maxWorkers: 4`, so up to four spawn-heavy test files start `tsx`
  concurrently; per-spawn cost rises well above the isolated ~3 s, which is
  how a 203 s test exceeds its 300 s budget.
- **Recurrence #3.** This test has already produced two closed test-failure
  items — WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S (worktree `tsx` ENOENT, fixed by
  `resolveTsxBin()`) and WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9 (10 s hook timeout → hook
  raised to 180 s, test to 300 s in commit `2e64aacf`). Both were
  timeout/wiring band-aids; the underlying spawn cost was never addressed,
  so the failure has now returned at the raised ceiling.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Check out `dev` (or the relevant worktree) with dependencies installed.
2. Run the failing test: `npm --silent test -- tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`
   (this is a TypeScript/vitest test — the `pytest -q -r a ... -k '<name>'`
   form in the auto-generated triage template does not apply to this file).
3. Observe either the 300 s `Test timed out` failure, or a 200 s+ pass on a
   less loaded machine; capture the test's own summary line
   `[spawn-reduction] panes=6 queries=5 baselineWork=… cachedWork=…
   cacheHits=… reduction=…% (target ≥60%)` from stdout.
4. For the contention path, run the full canonical suite
   (`npm --silent test -- tests/cli`) rather than the file in isolation —
   both prior occurrences passed in isolation and failed under suite load.

## Impact

The slowest single test in the repository (203 s, ~8% of aggregate suite
test-time) intermittently times out and turns `dev` red, blocking PR
creation and making every implement/test/audit gate flaky and slow. Because
the failure is a timeout rather than an assertion failure, re-running
"to confirm flakiness" (the standard triage step) burns another 3-10 minutes
without changing the outcome.

## Root cause analysis (hypothesis — to be confirmed during implementation)

- The read-cache logic is **not** implicated: the timeout pre-empts the
  `expect(cachedWork).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.4 * baselineWork)` assertion, and
  the same assertions passed on the finish-gate run that preceded the
  recorded failure.
- The dominant cost is **process startup, not cache behaviour**: 65 cold
  `tsx` starts inside one test, amplified by up to 4-way worker contention.
- **Timeouts have already been raised twice** (vitest default 30 s →
  180 s hook / 300 s test in `2e64aacf`). The measured wall clock has now
  outgrown the raised budget, so a third raise is not a fix: it moves the
  ceiling, lengthens every gate further, and leaves the flakiness in place.

## Approach options (implementer to evaluate — do not assume)

1. **Batch the query set per pane.** Drive all 5 herdr queries for a pane in
   a single `tsx` invocation via a small test-only driver, keeping each pane
   a separate process → 12 spawns instead of 60, preserving the
   cross-process property the test exists to measure.
2. **Reduce redundant work.** Seed via the existing helper/`cli-helpers.ts`
   paths rather than 5 separate `tsx create` subprocesses, and check whether
   the baseline and cached phases can share seeded state.
3. **In-process harness.** `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` exists and is used by
   several CLI tests. Viable **only** if it still exercises the
   cross-process *on-disk* cache (`WL_CACHE_DIR`, `src/read-cache.ts`): the
   whole point is that panes are separate processes sharing one cache
   directory, so an in-memory layer would make the ≥60% assertion vacuous.
   Note `recordSpawn` is invoked by CLI code (`src/cli.ts:560`,
   `src/read-cache-cli.ts:173/176`), so counters stay honest in-process.
4. **Long-run group.** Move to the `*.long.test.ts` convention only if none
   of the above preserves the measurement cheaply; record it explicitly as a
   deliberate coverage decision, not a silent skip.

## Constraints

- **No third timeout raise as the fix.** Justify with measurements if a
  budget change is made anyway.
- **Preserve the measurement's intent:** the test must keep asserting ≥60%
  fewer `read-work` spawns and >0 `cache-hit`s across panes sharing one cache
  directory. Any reduction in simulated panes or queries must be justified
  against the parent target (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA AC7: 6 panes, herdr's real
  query set) and recorded on this item.
- **No production-code change** unless a genuine cache defect is proven.
- **Coordinate, don't duplicate:** suite-wide test-speed optimisation is
  owned by WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 (in progress); this item's scope is making
  *this* test pass deterministically.
- Tests are run only through the standard test skill (`/skill:test`); no
  ad-hoc test invocation.
- Work lands on `dev` only, via the standard worktree/implement flow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts > read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) > cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh` passes against the latest `dev`, both in isolation and under the full-suite/parallel-load conditions that produced this failure.
- The test's runtime is reduced so it completes well inside its configured budget on a loaded host, and the achieved runtime (with the command and host conditions used) is recorded on this item.
- The ≥60% spawn-reduction assertion and the >0 cache-hit assertion are unchanged in intent, and any reduction in simulated panes or queries is justified against the parent target (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA AC7) and recorded on this item.
- No third timeout raise is used as the fix; if a timeout or hook budget is changed anyway, it is justified with before/after measurements and recorded on this item.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes, green on repeated CI-like runs without an intermittent timeout for this test.
- Related documentation is updated where it describes this test: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § "Spawn instrumentation (spawn-reduction measurement)", the test file's header comment, and code comments for any new helper.

## Key Files

**Key Files:** the files an implementer will touch — every path verified to exist on `dev` @ `bec96e2b`.

- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — the failing test: 6-pane simulation, `300_000` ms budget, 65 `tsx` spawns.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — `writeConfig`, `writeInitSemaphore` seeding helpers used by the test.
- `tests/test-utils.ts` — `createTempDir`, `cleanupTempDir`, `resolveTsxBin` (added by WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S).
- `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` — in-process CLI harness (option 3 above).
- `src/cli.ts` — read-cache env plumbing (`WL_CACHE_DISABLED`/`WL_CACHE_TTL_MS`/`WL_CACHE_DIR`, lines ~262-267) and the `recordSpawn('read-work')` baseline path (line ~560).
- `src/read-cache.ts` — on-disk shared cache (`WL_CACHE_DIR` precedence, line ~445).
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — `cache-hit` / `read-work` spawn recording (lines ~173-176).
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — `countSpawnRecords`, the assertion's data source.
- `./vitest.config.ts` — `pool: 'forks'`, `maxWorkers: 4`, `testTimeout`, long-run exclusions.
- `./package.json` — `test` and `test:timings` scripts.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — § "Spawn instrumentation (spawn-reduction measurement)" explicitly references this test.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8** (in progress, `plan_complete`) — "Reduce time to run
  tests". Names this test as the #1 offender (203 s) and owns the broader
  suite-speed work (baseline capture, mocking spawned `wl` processes,
  long-run grouping). **Overlap:** its AC3 (triage every test ≥5 s) and AC2
  (≥30% suite reduction) touch this test. This item stays the narrow,
  critical fix; anything broader (config changes, other slow files) belongs
  to that epic.
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** (completed) — prior occurrence; raised the hook to
  180 s and the test to 300 s (`2e64aacf`). Its band-aid is why the failure
  returned at the new ceiling.
- **WL-0MSGS55JL0006A4S** (completed) — prior occurrence; worktree `tsx`
  ENOENT, fixed by `resolveTsxBin()` in `tests/test-utils.ts`.
- **WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA** (completed) — created this test and its parent
  target (AC7: ≥60% spawn reduction across a 6-pane refresh).
- **WL-0MVGC6JVP00812DS** (in review) — the item whose post-push full-suite
  run surfaced this timeout; also surfaced WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U
  (`entry-point-split` version-record failure), a separate flake.
- Duplicate check performed: no completed item already makes this test pass
  deterministically (both prior occurrences closed on timeout/wiring
  band-aids, not cost), and the owning epic WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 is still in
  progress, so this item is **not** a duplicate — partial overlap recorded
  above.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the work item is an auto-generated
test-failure report (`[test-failure]`, priority critical) whose seed intent
(fix the named failing test) combined with the evidence above makes the
deliverable unambiguous. Derivations recorded instead:

- **Derived (no question needed).** The failure is a timeout, so the fix must
  address test cost/determinism, not cache behaviour. Evidence:

# Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) measured the sync persist phase at 83.6 s of an 85.9 s pipeline on the 123.7 MB fixture, with 78–90 % of the CPU inside `upsertFtsEntry`. `db.import()` clears every work item, re-saves every item and then re-indexes the FTS row of every item; `db.importComments()` clears every comment, re-saves every comment and re-indexes the FTS row of every item. A no-change sync therefore pays the whole cost. This item implements the fix behind parent ACs 1, 3 and 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `db.import()` writes only records whose merged value differs from the local store: unchanged work items/edges/audits are not re-saved, while `updatedAt` preservation and the later-`activityAt` merge still hold (an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted so no activity timestamp is lost).
- Records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (work items, comments, edges) and only those deleted ids have their FTS rows removed — `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` no longer force a full FTS rebuild, with existing callers (`importData()`, `doctor migrate`, `clear()`) keeping their current destructive behaviour.
- `db.importComments()` writes only changed/new comments and performs FTS upkeep only for the affected parent item ids — FTS maintenance is proportional to changed items, never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge (the delta `upsertComments()` path too: look up only the affected ids instead of scanning every item).
- Each record type is persisted inside one transaction (or batched statements): `db.importComments()` gains a transaction wrapping its clear/save/FTS work, no per-row transaction is introduced, and `db.import()`'s existing atomicity is preserved.
- Existing sync contracts still hold — delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results — and the existing sync and FTS tests plus the write-detection tests from the verification item stay green.

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits); a no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertItems()`, `upsertComments()`, `hasWorkItemChanged`/`compareTrackedFields`, `mergeAuditsNewestWins`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`, `saveWorkItem`, `transaction`.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist branch (delta via `upsertItems`/`upsertComments`, full snapshot via `import`/`importComments`).

## Dependencies

- Verify item (persist write-detection regression tests) — test-first.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `import()`: compute the diff against the existing snapshot — unchanged records (per `hasWorkItemChanged`) are skipped entirely (no `saveWorkItem`), changed/new records are saved, ids absent from the incoming set are deleted with only their FTS rows removed; keep the transaction and `updatedAt`/`activityAt` semantics.
- In `importComments()`: diff comments by identity fields, skip unchanged saves, delete removed comments, wrap clear/save/FTS in one transaction, and re-index FTS only for the affected parent ids.
- Reduce `upsertComments()` to look up only the affected parent ids (no full table scan) and confirm no full FTS rebuild remains after a comment merge.
- Preserve `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` for their remaining callers; introduce targeted FTS-row deletion for the sync path.

## Deliverables

- Rewritten persist path: writes and FTS work proportional to actually-changed records, transactions per record type, contracts unchanged.
data.title: Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

# Impl: sync phase-timing observability

## Background

The F2 stage harness replays `performSync`'s persist pipeline out of process because `wl sync` reports a single wall-clock number with no phase attribution. Parent AC 5 requires the pull/persist/export/push timings to be observable so a before/after breakdown can be reproduced with the documented commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `performSync` reports per-phase timings for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export and push as log lines and/or added `--json` fields.
- The F2 probe (`packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts`) uses the same phase names, so its output lines up with the in-CLI timings and the before/after table.
- A default-suite test asserts the timing fields/log lines are emitted (present and numeric) and that the existing `--json` sync response shape is unchanged apart from the added timing fields.
- Timing output is off/silent by default where it would pollute machine-readable output (added `--json` fields only, or verbose-only log lines), matching existing `wl sync` output conventions.

- Phase timings are observable (log lines and/or `--json` fields for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push) so the F2 stage harness can reproduce a before/after breakdown with the documented commands.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` phase boundaries and `--json` output.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts` — phase names to align with.
- `packages/herdr/src/wl-sync-phase-probe.test.ts` — probe phase coverage test.

## Dependencies

- Implementation item (change-detection persist) — phases are timed on the rewritten persist path.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a small phase-timer helper in `performSync` around the existing phase boundaries (pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push) that emits `--json` timing fields or verbose log lines.
- Align the probe's phase labels with the in-CLI names.
- Add a default-suite test driving `performSync` (dry-run / copied store) asserting the timing fields appear and the existing JSON response shape is unchanged apart from the additions.

## Deliverables

- Observable phase timings in `wl sync` (log and/or `--json`), aligned with the F2 probe, with a regression test.

# Measure and document: persist perf before/after

## Background

Parent ACs 2 and 6 require proof: the persist phase must drop to ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline on the 123.7 MB fixture, measured with the documented F2 commands, and the re-runnable commands plus a before/after table must land in the docs. `docs/DATA_SYNCING.md` named by the parent does not exist in this repo, so a `docs/dev/` note is the documentation home (the parent AC allows either), alongside the F2 `wl sync` persist section in `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Persist-phase time on the regenerated 123.7 MB F2 fixture (2,600 items / 26,000 comments) is ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline (57.4 s → ≤ 5.7 s for in-process `db.import` + `db.importComments`), measured with the documented harness and probe commands; the ratio and CPU-profile self-time shares are quoted (not a single wall number, which is load-sensitive).
- A no-change sync profile shows zero `upsertFtsEntry` self time.
- A `docs/dev/` note (e.g. `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md`) records the re-runnable commands and the before/after table; the `### wl sync persist phases` section of `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` is updated to record the fix instead of describing it as outstanding.
- The measurements, host context and timestamp are quoted in the parent item's completion comment.

- Persist-phase time on the 123.7 MB F2 fixture drops to ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline (57.4 s → ≤ 5.7 s in-process `db.import` + `db.importComments`), measured with the documented F2 commands and quoted in the completion comment.
- Docs updated (`DATA_SYNCING.md` and/or a `docs/dev/` note) with the re-runnable measurement commands and the before/after table.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — F1 fixture generator / F2 stage profile.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts` — persist-phase probe.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — F2's `wl sync` persist section.
- `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md` — new note (before/after table + commands).

## Dependencies

- Implementation item (change-detection persist) and the phase-timing item — the measurement needs both.

## Minimal Implementation

- Regenerate the F2 fixture (`large-db-harness.ts --profile full --stages --json`) and run the persist-phase probe before/after on disposable copies; record wall and CPU times plus `node --cpu-prof` self-time shares.
- Write `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md` with the commands and before/after table; update the F2 section in `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.
- Quote the before/after ratio and CPU shares in a comment on the parent item.

## Deliverables

- Verified ≤ 10 % persist-phase result (or documented blocker if the target is not met), docs update, and parent completion comment with evidence.
